label: PF Backlog 427
title: A2: capability registry + entitlement-at-boundary + asymmetric licensing
body: [A2] Capability registry; entitlement checks at execution boundaries; asymmetric license (public-key verify; private key never ships).

analysis.implementation_strategy: Reuse-first across the registry stack. Extend core/licensing.py to implement asymmetric (public-key) license verification: the shipped artifact embeds only the public key; licenses are signed offline with the private key which never ships. Extend core/capability_bridge.py and core/capability_packs.py so every capability resolution passes through an entitlement check at the execution boundary (reuse core/execution_contract.py as the boundary hook). Capability definitions stay in config/capability-packs.json and config/licensing-tiers.json (extend schema: add entitlement/feature flags per tier and public key fingerprint). Expose entitlements via the existing /api/v1/enterprise/tenants/{tenant}/entitlements and /api/v1/enterprise/tenants/{tenant}/license endpoints. The capability registry itself reuses core/change_registry.py patterns and core/knowledge_registry.py/config/plugins-registry.json conventions rather than a new store.

conflict_findings: BI-PF-0352 likely owns overlapping licensing/entitlement scope; assign ownership of the license format and key handling to one item before implementation starts to avoid conflicting edits to core/licensing.py.
core/capability_bridge.py and core/execution_contract.py may be touched by BI-PF-0438 (web_search tool, pluggable, default off) — entitlement gating of new tools must use the same boundary.
core/change_registry.py is shared with BI-PF-0395's classifier work.
duplication_findings: core/licensing.py already exists — this EXTENDS it with asymmetric verification, not a rewrite.
core/capability_bridge.py + core/capability_packs.py already model capabilities; the registry is the packs config plus an index, not a new component.
config/licensing-tiers.json and config/capability-packs.json already encode tiers/packs — extend, do not create parallel configs.
BI-PF-0352 (REL-0 packaging/licensing/entitlement) is the closest overlap (score 0.22): 0396 must be reconciled with it to avoid two licensing implementations — check for duplicate marking.
core/model_registry.py / core/artifact_registry.py show the registry pattern to follow; no new pattern needed.
analysis.rationale: Reuse-first: eight existing components and six config modules map directly onto this item; licensing and capability registries already exist and only need asymmetric verification plus boundary enforcement. No new component required. The primary risk is scope overlap with BI-PF-0352 (REL-0), which must be reconciled before coding.
assumptions: core/licensing.py exists and currently handles some license check that can be extended.
Tenant-scoped entitlements API endpoints exist and can be backed by the extended licensing module.
Capabilities are enumerated in config/capability-packs.json and can carry entitlement flags.
The private key is held only in the release-signing environment, not in the repo.
risks: Key management mistakes (private key leaking into the artifact) — mitigate with a build-time assertion/test that scans the artifact for the private key and for key material outside the public key.
License format drift vs REL-0 (BI-PF-0352) if both proceed independently — mitigate via dedup/reconciliation decision.
Entitlement checks at every boundary may add latency; cache entitlement results per tenant with TTL.
Offline/air-gapped license verification (grace/expiry without clock) needs design.
Public-key algorithm choice (Ed25519 vs RSA) affects artifact size and verify speed.
evidence: candidate components: core/licensing.py, core/capability_bridge.py, core/capability_packs.py, core/execution_contract.py, core/change_registry.py, core/knowledge_registry.py, core/model_registry.py, core/artifact_registry.py

brief.problem: Commercial editions need capability gating and licensing that cannot be tampered with or leak the private key.
brief.what_adds: A2 — capability registry + entitlement checks at execution boundaries + asymmetric licensing (public-key verify; the private key never ships).
brief.why: Enforce edition entitlements at runtime and protect licenses from forgery.
brief.who_feels: PF platform maintainers, workers, and customers.
